title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript leaf. It is a typescript page (p. 84 of Exposé IX) of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie' (Grothendieck, 1967-69; LNM 288, 1972), filed among the 1975-76 notes on the divided-power De Rham complex. The neighbouring handwritten pages, on truncation functors τ_N, φ_{N,ω} and Ext vanishing, are unrelated.

Setting of §7. S = Spec V, with V noetherian, separated and complete for an ideal m; S_0 = V(m). A is a smooth group scheme over S whose restriction A_0 to S_0 has identity component an extension of an abelian scheme by a torus. The formal completion of A along S_0 then yields a formal abelian scheme \hat B over the formal completion of S.

Proposition 7.1.5. If S is normal, \hat B is algebraizable, and the abelian scheme B over S that it comes from is projective.

Proof sketch:
1. Reduce to A = A^o with S integral.
2. Raynaud (Faisceaux amples sur les schémas en groupes, LNM 119, XI 1.13): a smooth group scheme with connected fibres over a normal base is quasi-projective. So choose a relatively ample invertible sheaf L.
3. Form the birigidified sheaf δ(L) = m^*L ⊗ pr_1^*L^{-1} ⊗ pr_2^*L^{-1} on A×_S A (the Mumford Λ(L) construction).
4. The unipotent rank of the fibres is zero over S_0. By semicontinuity (3.1) it is zero everywhere, since every point of Spec V specializes into V(m).
5. By VIII 7.5, δ(L) is then a biextension W of (A,A) by G_m. W is symmetric, and by VIII 4.13 (essentially Raynaud XI 1.11) it satisfies the ampleness condition at the points of S_0.
6. The earlier criterion of §7.1 then yields a polarization of \hat B. Grothendieck's formal existence theorem algebraizes \hat B to a projective abelian scheme.

Remark 7.1.6 says normality can be removed by reducing to the normal case as in 13.5.3 a).

Lemma 7.2.1 begins the setup for the next step. Its category C consists of smooth finite-type group schemes over the complete base with A/A^o étale finite and A^o an extension of an abelian scheme by an isotrivial torus. This prepares the comparison with formal groups used in the semi-stable reduction and monodromy theory of SGA 7 IX.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. The step 'unipotent rank zero on A_0 implies zero on A' tacitly uses that every point of Spec V specializes into V(m) (m lies in the Jacobson radical by completeness). This is standard and is what 'résulte facilement de 3.1' covers.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the published SGA 7 I Exposé IX typescript, misfiled among the De Rham notes. All its content is published and credited. The only curiosity is archival: a 1960s SGA typescript sits inside cote 136.
transcription_corrections: The page is typescript, not handwriting. It is SGA 7 Exposé IX p. 84, unrelated to the surrounding handwritten pages.
'A_o' and 'S_o' are A_0 and S_0 (subscript zero), the restrictions to V(m).
The handwritten '407' at the bottom, the stamped '402' and the pencilled '265' are archival page numbers, not mathematics.
